trust.title: Trust at a glance
items: All consultations and guidance are free
We reply by email within 1–2 business days (info@hapvi.org)
trust.privacyNote: Information you submit is used only for consultation purposes.

items.a: Yes. Housing and benefits guidance from HapVi Together is free. Donations are voluntary and not required to receive help.

items.q: Can you help if I struggle with English?
items.a: Yes. We explain steps in Korean. Official application sites are often in English—we help you understand what to click and what documents are needed.

items.q: What if my immigration status is uncertain?
items.a: You can still request a consultation. Each agency makes the final decision; we do not determine eligibility—we connect you to official sites and explain the process.

items.q: Who decides if I qualify for benefits?
items.a: Government agencies make official determinations. We link to official application portals and offer Korean-language guidance.
Request a free consultation, or open our Benefits Guide and visit the official site for programs that interest you.

items.q: Do you serve areas outside Los Angeles?
items.a: We focus on Korean-American families in LA; many programs are LA County or California based. Tell us where you live and we will look for applicable resources together.

hero.title:
We began inside
this community.
hero.description:
The United States offers many housing and social supports for lower-income families.
Yet language barriers, complicated processes, and not knowing whom to ask leave many Korean-American households without benefits they’re entitled to.

HapVi Together was founded within the LA Korean community to close that gap.

Like our name—Happy Village Together—
building a better village together is where we start.

paragraphs: HapVi blends “Happy” and “Village,” reflecting our vision of a village where everyone can thrive.
The name is more than words—it’s a promise toward a better tomorrow.
Change begins with each of us.
Through education, housing, and healthier environments, HapVi Together helps individuals and families live fuller lives.
Together, we can build a stronger village and a sustainable future.
Now—let’s build a happier village together.

Eligibility.title: Government Benefits Guide
Eligibility.metaDescription: Official application links for Section 8, CalFresh, Medi-Cal, LIHEAP, and emergency rental assistance for LA Korean-American families.
Eligibility.intro: Click each benefit below to visit the official application site. Please check your eligibility directly on each official site.

benefitCards.title: Housing Voucher (Section 8 / HCV)
benefitCards.description: A federal program that helps low-income families afford safe, decent housing in the private market.

benefitCards.title: CalFresh (SNAP Food Assistance)
benefitCards.description: California's food assistance program that provides an EBT card for purchasing groceries.

benefitCards.title: Medi-Cal (Health Coverage)
benefitCards.description: California's health insurance program providing free or low-cost medical coverage for low-income residents.

benefitCards.title: LIHEAP (Utility Assistance)
benefitCards.description: A federal program that helps with electricity and gas bills. Check the official site for current availability.

benefitCards.title: Emergency Rental Assistance
benefitCards.description: Emergency assistance for households facing eviction or unpaid rent. Check the official site for current availability.

s1Items: Name and contact information (phone number or email)
s2Items: To provide housing support and public benefits counseling
To share service information and follow up with you
s3Items: We retain records for three years after a consultation is completed

s4Items: We do not share your information with third parties as a rule
Exceptions may apply where required by law
